messages:
omar: heads-up: found a weird parity bug between node/python sampleapps hitting embeddings + rerank. node helper uses `Float32Array.subarray()` to slice buffers and in one run the last float was dropped -> server returned `400 vector-length-mismatch`. sampleapp then retried entire batch and created duplicate items in the index.

omar: minimal repro (node):
```js
const view = new Float32Array(buf.buffer, offset, len);
// subarray used later: view.subarray(0, len-1) accidentally in one branch
```

rita: interesting. subarray can create a view w/o copying; bug likely in an off-by-one when computing end index. python path makes copies so never hit it.

leo: two things we should do: 1) add strict client-side dim validation in both SDKs (throw or opt-in pad/truncate); 2) narrow retry policy in sampleapp so structural 4xx (vector-dim-mismatch) aren't retried.

omar: also noticed rerank responses differed: node wrapper returned `vector_id` fields, python returned `id`. led to dedupe mismatch after retry. we should normalize server->sdk to always provide `id`. filed SDK issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/479

build-bot: created ticket DEVEX-1210: "vector-slice off-by-one in node helper + retry UX"

ci-bot: leo opened PR #814: "js-sdk: validate vector dims before send; expose validationMode". tests queued.

rita: short-term local workaround: a preflight check `if (vec.length !== expected) throw` and a small script to diff node/python outputs. don't pad silently.

leo: ops note: duplicate submissions from retry loops can inflate usage metrics. tagging billing team to audit spikes. :money_with_wings:

omar: i'll attach a tiny failing gist and a unit test that reproduces the subarray path. will follow up with PR to sampleapp to change retry rules. thanks all. :rocket:
